Playful indicators

Source: vignettes/articles/playful.Rmd
playful.Rmd

Illustrative, animated SVG indicators. Each one shows a single level and is meant for presentations, landing pages and dashboards that need a lighter touch. They come to life when they scroll into view: the heart and the glass fill up, the plant, the hair and the nose grow, the flame ignites and the flower blooms, while the value counts up. They only animate while they are on screen, and they stay still for visitors who have asked their system for reduced motion.

Every indicator reacts to the mouse, and the heart, the glass, the plant, the hair, the nose and the flame can be made draggable = TRUE. Viewers can then set the level themselves by dragging, or with the arrow keys. In Shiny, the new level arrives in input$<id>_value, and clicks arrive in input$<id>_clicked.

Chart Use it when
heart_fill() You show a level from 0 to 1 as a beating heart filling with liquid
glass_fill() You show a level from 0 to 1 as a glass of water
plant_growth() You show progress as a plant that grows and blooms
hair_growth() You show progress as hair growing from bald to a big afro
nose_growth() You show a growing number, such as unchecked claims, as a nose that keeps growing
flame() You show an intensity, such as an error count, as a flame
flower() You want a blooming flower, or a small flower chart of a few values

heart_fill()

heart_fill() shows a level from 0 to 1 as a heart filling with a wavy liquid. The heart beats, and the percentage written inside turns white where the liquid covers it. Hover the heart to make it beat faster, and click it to release a few small hearts. target marks a level to reach.

heart_fill(fill_level = 0.8, title_text = NULL)
heart_fill(
  fill_level = 0.45,
  target = 0.75,
  fill_color = "#ff8ab7",
  stroke_color = "#c2185b",
  title_text = "Daily activity goal"
)

With draggable = TRUE, drag the heart up or down to set the level:

heart_fill(0.3, draggable = TRUE, title_text = "Drag the heart", bpm = 80)

glass_fill()

glass_fill() shows the level as a glass of water, with a moving surface and rising bubbles. Move the mouse across the chart to rock the water, and click the glass to drop some more in. ticks = TRUE adds a measuring scale.

glass_fill(fill_level = 0.8, title_text = "Glass of water")
glass_fill(
  fill_level = 0.35,
  target = 0.8,
  ticks = TRUE,
  title_text = "Water intake today"
)
glass_fill(0.6, fill_color = "#efb118", draggable = TRUE, title_text = "Drag the water")

plant_growth()

plant_growth() shows progress as a potted plant. As the level grows, the plant goes from a seed to a sprout, grows leaves, forms a bud from 55 percent and opens into a flower at 100 percent. The current stage is written under the percentage. Hover the plant to stir up the breeze, and click it to water it.

plant_growth(0.4)
plant_growth(1, title_text = "Project completed")
plant_growth(
  0.7,
  target = 0.9,
  pot_color = "#4269d0",
  flower_color = "#efb118",
  draggable = TRUE,
  title_text = "Drag the plant"
)

hair_growth()

hair_growth() shows progress as a portrait whose hair grows with the level. At 0 the person is bald, with a shiny head; the hair then goes through stubble, a buzz cut, short curls and curly hair, and becomes a big afro, with an afro pick, at 100 percent. The person smiles more as the hair grows, and the current stage is written under the percentage. The eyes follow the mouse; click the portrait to make the afro bounce and get a wink. target draws a dashed outline of the hair to reach.

hair_growth(1, title_text = "Fully grown")
hair_growth(0.35, target = 0.8, title_text = "Fundraising goal")

With draggable = TRUE, drag up to grow the hair and down to cut it. The colours of the hair, the skin, the turtleneck and the card can all be changed:

hair_growth(
  0.6,
  hair_color = "#6b3e26",
  skin_color = "#f1c7a5",
  shirt_color = "#3ca951",
  panel_color = "#fdf1e3",
  draggable = TRUE,
  title_text = "Drag up or down"
)

nose_growth()

nose_growth() shows a level as a person in profile whose nose grows longer and longer, like the nose of a teller of tall tales. The nose reaches across the chart at 100 percent; a twig with leaves sprouts from it above 62 percent and a bird lands on it above 92 percent (leaves, bird). The person looks more and more nervous as the nose grows, and the stage goes from “Honest” to “Pants on fire”. The eye follows the mouse, the ponytail swings, and clicking the portrait makes the nose wobble while the person protests in a speech bubble.

nose_growth(1, title_text = "Pants on fire")
nose_growth(0.3, target = 0.7, title_text = "Claims not yet fact-checked")

With draggable = TRUE, drag right to grow the nose and left to shrink it: the tip follows the mouse. The colours of the skin, the hair, the stripes and the card can be changed:

nose_growth(
  0.55,
  skin_color = "#8d5a3b",
  hair_color = "#1f1a17",
  shirt_color = "#c0392b",
  panel_color = "#fdf1e3",
  draggable = TRUE,
  title_text = "Drag the nose"
)

flame()

flame() shows an intensity as a flickering flame. This is useful for a critical number, such as the number of errors in a process. The flame grows linearly with the intensity up to max_intensity (100 by default). The higher the intensity, the faster it flickers and the more sparks it throws. The flame leans away from the mouse, and flares up when clicked. It can burn on its own, on a candle or on logs.

flame(
  intensity = 35,
  base = "candle",
  show_value = TRUE,
  value_suffix = " errors",
  title_text = "Failed jobs today"
)
flame(
  intensity = 80,
  flame_gradient_colors = c("#e0f7ff", "#5ac8fa", "#1d4ed8"),
  bg_col = "#111111",
  base = "logs"
)
flame(intensity = 20, draggable = TRUE, show_value = TRUE, title_text = "Drag the flame")

flower()

flower() draws a flower that blooms when it comes into view and then turns slowly. Click a petal to pluck it, and the flower says “loves me” or “loves me not”. When the last petal falls, the verdict is shown and the flower grows back. Click the centre to make it grow back at any time.

flower(petal_count = 7, petal_color = "plum", rotation_speed = 0)
flower(
  petal_count = 14,
  petal_color = "#efb118",
  center_color = "#5b3a29",
  center_stroke = "#3b2416",
  center_text = "14",
  center_text_color = "white",
  rotation_speed = 0.3
)

With petal_values, the flower becomes a small chart. There is one petal per value, its length is proportional to the value, and hovering a petal shows its value and share. Clicking a petal highlights it.

flower(
  petal_values = c(8, 6, 9, 4, 7, 5),
  petal_labels = c("Speed", "Power", "Skill", "Luck", "Focus", "Stamina"),
  value_suffix = " / 10",
  title_text = "Player profile"
)
